description: Small category reference derived from app data and benchmark-oriented manual additions.

entries.notes: If there is a warning, scan the material clues and whether the cup is grease-resistant, waterproof, lined, or foam-based.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Look for product name, lining claims, compostable claims, water-resistant claims, or California warning text.

entries.notes: Packaging warnings often need material context; the same warning means different things on foam, paperboard, or molded fiber.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Ask whether it is foam, paperboard, molded fiber, or plastic-lined.

entries.notes: Soft wipe-clean layers matter more than plain cotton fabric.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Look for wipe-clean, PVC, vinyl, coated, waterproof claims.

entries.notes: Material construction matters more than the textile name alone.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Look for waterproof, stain-resistant, wipe-clean, vinyl-like descriptions.

entries.notes: Vinyl-like or heavily treated soft goods deserve more follow-up than plain woven fabric.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Look for PVC, vinyl, mildew-resistant, waterproof claims.

entries.notes: For furniture, engineered wood emissions can matter more than decorative textile surfaces.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Ask whether the item uses MDF, particleboard, plywood, or composite wood.

entries.notes: Brightly dyed or treated textiles raise different questions than plain undyed fiber.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Look for stain-resistant, water-repellent, anti-odor, easy-clean, intensely dyed fabric.

entries.notes: For items meant for mouthing, toy-specific migration and content limits matter.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Check age range, mouthing use, plasticized parts, paint, finger-paint-like or liquid toy materials.

entries.notes: Ingredient-list matching matters more than product category alone.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Scan the ingredient list and any active ingredients or preservatives.

entries.notes: A Prop 65 warning alone does not tell the user exposure level, route, or whether ordinary use is high risk.
entries.what_to_ask_or_scan_next: Scan the full warning text, product type, and any named chemicals.

entries.notes: Use ingredient-first reasoning for ordinary foods and beverages.
Supplements should still follow ingredient-first reasoning even when marketed like wellness products.
Ceramic food-contact products depend heavily on material and decoration clues.
For cleaners and sprays, ingredients and label handling cautions matter most.
Electronics often depend more on accessible material and plastic components than a named ingredient list.
